newsitem.title: MONACO: TENNIS-BECKER CRASHES OUT IN MONTE CARLO.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER CRASHES OUT IN MONTE CARLO.

text.p: Boris Becker crashed out of the Monte Carlo Open on Tuesday, losing to Italy's Renzo Furlan in the first round of his favourite claycourt tournament.

Back on clay for the first time in a season so far marred by injuries, Becker made a promising start but soon found it too difficult to adapt to the slow surface and bowed out 1-6 6-3 7-6 in just over two hours.

The loss may not be a surprise since Becker, ranked 12th in the world, only resumed playing in Tokyo last week after a two-month break because of a tendinitis. He had also complained of thigh pains in Tokyo.
But the defeat, in only his sixth match this year, was a further disappointment for the German, who has lost three finals in Monte Carlo.
"He was very good in the first set, especially at the net. And then he started playing poorly and I realised I only needed to play solid tennis," said Furlan, ranked 65 in the world.
The first set went smoothly for Becker but everything changed in the second set.
The German suddenly served poorly -- his first serve percentage reached a miserable 23 percent -- allowing Furlan back into the match.
Becker seemed to recover, leading 3-0 in the final set, but his game again fell apart for no obvious reason and Furlan levelled at 4-4 and earned a deserved tie break.
Becker collapsed completely, trailing Furlan 4-0, and only managed to save one match point before crashing out on a backhand volley.
"It's a big disappointment because I was so close to win but to be so close to win when I served so poorly was a surprise," he said.
The German was the first major casualty in the tournament, even though other favourites had hiccups in their first matches on clay this season.
Ukrainian Andrei Medvedev, winner here in 1994 but unseeded this year, had to fight for three sets to dismiss Swede Nicklas Kulti 4-6 6-2 6-3.
Two other Spaniards had a much easier day. Twelfth seed Alex Corretja beat Portugal's Ninos Marques 6-0 6-0 while compatriot Felix Mantilla, seeded 11th, beat Czech Martin Damm 6-1 6-1 in 36 minutes.
